title: Rational and algebraically closed stages
statement:
Use the finite-field and coefficient setting of [def-sf-datum]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and a separated finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ of finite-type $k$-schemes. Use the completed integral operations and their rational and common-stage extensions [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and the projection transformation [def-sf-pf, def-exchange-projection]. Let $K_0\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and $L_0\in D^b_c(Y,R)$ be integral objects in the derived-complete sense [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $K=Q_XK_0$, $L=Q_YL_0$ in the raw rationalized categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Then
$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes_E^L L\longrightarrow Rf_!(K\otimes_E^L Lf^*L)
$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $K,L$ and compatible with rationalization and finite scalar extension. The same assertion holds over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ for objects represented by such objects over a common finite coefficient field, in the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], independently of that presentation. Compatibility with finite reduction means the following statement about the chosen integral representatives: $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_0,L_0}$ reduces to $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_{0,n},L_{0,n}}$ for $K_{0,n}=K_0\otimes_R^L R/\varpi_E^n$, $L_{0,n}=L_0\otimes_R^L R/\varpi_E^n$, compatibly for all $n\geq1$, and its rationalization is the displayed field-stage map. No reduction of a field-coefficient object independent of its integral representative is asserted.

proof.text: Fix the objects and morphism in the statement. The geometric and coefficient hypotheses are those of [def-sf-datum]. First apply [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] to $K_0$ on $X$ and to $L_0$ on $Y$: these are derived-complete bounded constructible integral objects and $\ell$ is invertible, so that lemma gives $D^b_c(-,R)=D^b_{ctf}(-,R)$ and the uniform finite-level Tor intervals. Thus $K_0,L_0$ satisfy exactly the derived-complete finite-Tor hypotheses of [thm-sf-pf-adic], without an additional hypothesis on the chosen integral models. Apply that theorem to obtain an isomorphism $p_0=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_0,L_0}$, with inverse $b_0$, and its compatible finite reductions. Throughout, $\operatorname{PF}$ denotes the specified projection transformation of [def-sf-pf]. This uses the integral projection theorem, not axiom (A3) asserting the desired projection formula at the field stage.

source.place: first paragraph: apply the integral theorem before rationalization

proof.text: Let $Q_W:D^b_c(W,R)\to D^b_c(W,E)$ be the scalar localization in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. By [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] the rational pullback and tensor are the localized completed integral operations, and by [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] rational compact support is the localized integral compact support. The coefficient comparisons preserve the tensor maps and the actual units and counits by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Consequently the composite defining the projection map in [def-exchange-projection] localizes to the corresponding composite over $E$: if $f=pj$ is the chosen compactification, its two factors $\pi_{p;j_!K_0,L_0}$ and $Rp_*(\gamma_{K_0,L_0})$ localize to their rational factors. Under the resulting source and target comparisons, $p_E=Q_Y(p_0)=p_0\otimes1$. Its inverse is $Q_Y(b_0)$: $Q_Y(b_0)Q_Y(p_0)=Q_Y(b_0p_0)=1$ and $Q_Y(p_0)Q_Y(b_0)=1$. Thus this is the specified field-stage projection map, not just an unspecified isomorphism between its endpoints. Preservation of inverses uses only the functor laws.

source.place: first paragraph: localization of operations and of the projection composite; preservation of its inverse

proof.text: Naturality extends to every rational morphism, not only to integral ones. In [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] each Hom group is $\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,-)\otimes_RE$, the morphism formulas for pullback and tensor in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] extend linearly in each input, and the rational compact support of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], whose value on a rational object is the integral value regarded in the scalar localization, acts on a rational arrow $u\otimes a$ by $Rf_!(u)\otimes a$. For the two bifunctors $U_E(K,L)=Rf_!K\otimes_E^L L$ and $V_E(K,L)=Rf_!(K\otimes_E^L Lf^*L)$, integral naturality from [def-exchange-projection] says $V_0(u,v)p_{0,K,L}=p_{0,K',L'}U_0(u,v)$. Tensor this equality with $ab$ to obtain $V_E(u\otimes a,v\otimes b)p_{E,K,L}=p_{E,K',L'}U_E(u\otimes a,v\otimes b)$. Additivity proves the equality for sums of pure tensors, hence all rational arrows. For specified rational isomorphisms presenting the same objects, this equality identifies the two projection maps by the induced isomorphisms of source and target; their inverse maps agree too, since an inverse is unique.

source.place: first paragraph: naturality and independence of rational integral presentation, expanded by linearity

proof.text:
For a finite extension $E\subset F$ inside the fixed algebraic closure, write $T=-\otimes_EF$. Set $U_E(K,L)=Rf_{!,E}K\otimes_E^L L$ and $V_E(K,L)=Rf_{!,E}(K\otimes_E^L Lf_E^*L)$. The operation comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] give source and target isomorphisms $c_U:T U_E(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}U_F(TK,TL)$ and $c_V:T V_E(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}V_F(TK,TL)$. That lemma preserves precisely the tensor comparisons, units and counits appearing in the defining composite [def-exchange-projection]. Apply this to its first factor $\pi_p=Rp_*( (\varepsilon_p\otimes1)\mu_p)\eta_p$ and then its second factor $Rp_*(\gamma)$; composing the two resulting squares cancels the intermediate comparison and gives
$$c_V\,T(p_{E,K,L})=p_{F,TK,TL}\,c_U.$$
Thus $p_{F,TK,TL}=c_VT(p_{E,K,L})c_U^{-1}$, and its inverse is $c_UT(p_{E,K,L}^{-1})c_V^{-1}$. The identity and tower coherence use the coherent coefficient comparison data specified in [def-exchange-projection] with the composition identifications of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. In particular the same equation holds after any further common finite extension. Only the coefficient-comparison assertion of the lemma is used; invertibility at field coefficients has already been proved in Step 2.

source.place: last sentence: compatibility of the finite-stage system with scalar extension, expanded on both factors of PF

proof.text: For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, choose a common finite field $F$ representing the two inputs. This is possible by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], taking a compositum if the initial fields differ. Form the projection map at that stage using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]; in [def-exchange-projection] its common-stage morphism class is the algebraically closed projection map. Step 2 gives $p_F^{-1}$. In the common-stage Hom groups the two composites $[p_F^{-1}][p_F]=[1]$ and $[p_F][p_F^{-1}]=[1]$ are represented by the corresponding equalities already over $F$. Thus the projection class is invertible. Step 4 identifies this class with the one obtained after enlarging $F$. For different specified presentations or representatives of input arrows, pass to a common finite overfield where the presenting equalities hold, as in the displayed Hom-colimit definition. Step 3 gives naturality there and Step 4 commutes with further extensions; taking classes gives equality independently of the chosen common stage. For inverse classes the same conclusion follows either from the transported inverse formula in Step 4 or from uniqueness of an inverse. No infinite scalar-extension theorem for ambient derived categories is used.

source.place: second paragraph: construction of the algebraically closed map and inverse over a common finite stage

proof.text: Finally keep the chosen integral representatives $K_0,L_0$. The finite-reduction clause of [thm-sf-pf-adic] identifies the reductions of $p_0$ with the actual maps $p_n=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_{0,n},L_{0,n}}$, compatibly with all transition maps. The comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identify their endpoints and preserve the maps defining the projection composite [def-exchange-projection]. Step 2 identifies $Q_Y(p_0)$ with $p_E$, and Step 5 takes that finite-field map to its algebraically closed morphism class. This gives exactly the stated compatibility with finite reduction of the integral representative. No functor from rational or algebraically closed coefficients to finite coefficients is used: the two comparisons start at $p_0$, one going to its reductions and one to its rationalization. Replacing an integral representative gives the same field map by Step 3, but does not assert equality of the different integral reductions.

source.place: first paragraph and final compatibility clause: finite reductions belong to integral representatives

split_report.summary: Expanded the integral-to-rational-to-common-stage proof using existing operation coefficient comparisons, explicit inverse formulas, fractional naturality, and representative-aware finite reduction. No new nodes. Exact project attachment rejected because the Lean rational theorem explicitly omits finite scalar extension and the common-stage category. Clarified the finite-reduction clause, which cannot mean reduction of a rational object without an integral model; used the existing integral residue-Tor theorem to obtain the required finite-Tor bounds without restricting integral representatives. Did not invoke field-stage axiom (A3) or use coefficient compatibility as an uncited theorem.

The inherited sk-thm-sf-pf-field unit record has the older rationalization route, also realized by these steps; the current broader sketch unit has additional localizing/PBC claims, which this subordinate node does not state.

tool_uses.why: Generic DVR coefficient residue test gives uniform finite-Tor bounds for all integral constructible representatives, allowing application of the integral projection theorem without narrowing the field-stage statement.

Generic coefficient comparisons for pullback, tensor, compact support, units and counits; they identify the specified projection maps under rationalization and finite scalar extension. The item unit supplies no such comparison theorem.

Generic composition identifications for coefficient transition functors used when taking common finite overfields; this is coefficient-category coherence, not a replacement of the integral projection-formula route.
